messages:
sam: Heads-up — onboarding weights for `ultra-chat-8k` uploaded to gs://redwood-weights/ultra-chat/2026-03-14/v1. Quick check: the tokenizer appears to be inserting a hidden start token which shifts template token indices and breaks our function-calling mapping. ping @li @anya for a quick triage.

li: yep saw the same locally. the model manifest has `add_start_token: true` (legacy conversion default). that flag causes the extra token. we should validate manifests on ingest.

anya: quick repro I ran:
```python
from rwtoken import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_pretrained('ultra-chat-8k')
print(t.encode("User: hi\nAssistant:"))
# -> [1, 34, 78, 5, 2]  # note leading 1 (start) that our templates don't expect
```

mike: OK — two actionable items: 1) add a manifest lint in onboarding to catch `add_start_token` / `start_token_id` / `pad_token` mismatches, 2) add a unit test that tokenizes the chat template and asserts offsets (round-trip check).

sam: created PR https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/342 to add a manifest validator and a sample round-trip test. tagging infra-model-onboard.

kevin: FYI the dedicated runtime expects `model.tokens.start_included=false` semantics. if manifest says true we'll double-insert the start token at serve-time and the KV cache offsets will be wrong -> coherent cache misses. can the runtime map the manifest flag to the serving config automatically?

li: the runtime actually supports an override `tokenizer.start_included_override` (internal flag) but the console doesn't expose it. I'll add a small adapter to translate `add_start_token` -> runtime override during model load and open a UX ticket to show it in the Console.

deploy-bot: manifest-lint job deployed to staging (job id c3f2). summary: checked 7 new manifests, 2 flagged (ultra-chat-8k v1, vendor-compat/test-model). logs: https://ci.redwood/integrations/c3f2/logs

anya: small gotcha: trailing newline in our chat template tokenizes to a control token (198) for this tokenizer and in some templates that collides with sentinel parsing. workaround is to use explicit markers like `<|user|>` and strip trailing whitespace before tokenizing.

mike: can you add that whitespace-trim to the template helper? low-risk change. @anya can you review?

anya: on it, adding trim + clearer error message when token offsets don't match template placeholders. left a comment on PR 342 about the message text.

sam: plan: merge validator PR, run manifest-lint across recent uploads, add runtime adapter mapping, and follow up to expose override in Console. target ETA: EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

li: ack, will add the adapter and a short migration note for Dedicated teams.

kevin: thanks all — let me know if you want me to roll the runtime patch to staging after the adapter lands.

sam: will do. thanks everyone.
